what_its_for: Clindamycin palmitate is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, skin, female reproductive organs, and internal organs. It works by stopping the growth of bacteria. It will NOT work for viral infections like the common cold or flu.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a liquid (oral solution) that you swallow by mouth. Use the measuring spoon, oral syringe, or cup that comes with the medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon, as it may give you the wrong amount. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Take it at evenly spaced times throughout the day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Always finish the entire course of antibiotics, even if you start feeling better early.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your weight, age, and the type of infection being treated. A common dose for children is 8 to 25 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into 3 or 4 equal doses. For adults, a typical dose ranges from 150 to 450 mg every 6 to 8 hours. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose without talking to your doctor or pharmacist first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can increase the risk of side effects.
storage: Store the unmixed dry granules (powder) at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Once the pharmacist mixes the powder into a liquid, store it at room temperature — do NOT refrigerate the mixed liquid, as it may become too thick to pour. The mixed liquid is good for 2 weeks. Discard any unused liquid after 2 weeks. Keep all medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antidiarrheal medicines (such as loperamide or Imodium) without talking to your doctor first, especially if you develop diarrhea while taking this medication. Avoid sharing this medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Do not skip doses or stop taking it early, even if you feel better. Avoid taking other antibiotics at the same time unless your doctor tells you to.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe or persistent diarrhea, bloody or watery stools, stomach cramps (these could be signs of a serious bowel problem called C. difficile colitis); skin rash, hives, or itching; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; difficulty breathing or swallowing (signs of a severe allergic reaction); yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual tiredness or dark-colored urine. Also call your doctor if your symptoms are not improving after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting treatment. However, it is very important to finish all of your medication as prescribed, even if you feel completely better before it is gone. Stopping early can allow bacteria to survive and come back, possibly making the infection harder to treat.
special_populations: Children: This liquid form is often used for children because it is easier to swallow than capsules. The dose is carefully calculated based on body weight, so always confirm the correct dose with your child's doctor. Older adults: Use with caution; your doctor may monitor you more closely for digestive side effects. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as it may pass into breast milk. Kidney or liver problems: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
